deepdive.sec: Rotating Electrical Machines — Generators for Gas/Steam/Hydro Prime Movers (power-gen capital equipment)

bull_bear.body:
- Strong cash INR1.99 bn maintained.
- DFPS subsidiary investment fully provided/written down (clean-up).
- Retained earnings being consumed by working capital to fund growth (inventory build for short-cycle orders → converts to cash next quarter); EBITDA→CFO conversion ~21%, expected to improve.
- Trade receivables outpaced sales growth; CFO stated the ~INR700 cr outstanding has since been fully collected.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- Very high factory utilization → equipment-breakdown risk could cause delivery delays (the "new normal" pressure point).
- Customer concentration on a handful of prime-mover OEMs (INNIO, Baker Hughes/Brush, etc.); demand entirely derivative of OEM capacity adds (1 turbine = 1 generator).
- Commodity (copper) spikes outrunning hedges/PVC clauses.
- Execution/logistics (Turkey LD demonstrates downside of in-scope shipping).
- Large-generator ramp dependent on 15-16 month machine-tool delivery — slip risk; revenue contribution only FY29.
- NPCIL/nuclear domestic orders slow and choppy; competition from BHEL, Crompton, imports — no monopoly.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: - Confident, candid, controlled. MD repeatedly defers specifics ("answer in 3 months") on large generators and customer-share questions — disciplined, occasionally guarded. Transparent on the Turkey one-off and copper risk. Notable governance step: first-ever CEO hire (Deepak, ex-L&T Mitsubishi & GE) as #2 — explicit move to "professionalize" management as the company scales. Tone overall buoyant ("buoyant market in all segments," "focus is execution").
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- TDPS is structurally a "picks-and-shovels" beneficiary of prime-mover OEM capacity doubling by 2030 — 1:1 generator-to-turbine/engine ratio means TDPS volume mechanically tracks OEM expansion; no new generator entrants possible (limited prime-mover base).
- A signed capacity-commitment agreement with INNIO through 2030 (numbers undisclosed but "extremely good") de-risks a large chunk of the gas-engine ramp.
- The large-generator move (up to 200MW) is a TAM step-change competing directly with Siemens, Baker Hughes/Brush, Mitsubishi, Fuji, Toshiba — but monetizes only FY29; near-term it's an optionality story, not earnings.
- SpaceX named as a delivery destination — a marquee data-center/power reference.
- Working-capital intensity is the real constraint on growth, not demand or capacity.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Consolidated balance sheet as on Jun-26 shows Total Equity of Rs 11,579.21 Mn (Mar-26: Rs 10,717.64 Mn) against current Borrowings of Rs 238.10 Mn (Mar-26: Rs 180.96 Mn), with no non-current borrowings line disclosed.
- Cash and cash equivalents of Rs 1,196.20 Mn plus bank balances other than cash of Rs 1,203.02 Mn as on Jun-26; quarterly Finance Cost of Rs 1.92 Mn versus Other Income - Interest of Rs 25.68 Mn.
- Capital Work-in-Progress of Rs 197.34 Mn (Mar-26: Rs 173.25 Mn) and Intangible assets under development of Rs 90.29 Mn (Mar-26: Rs 100.54 Mn) are the only reinvestment line items shown; no capex plan or dividend policy is stated.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body:
- **Steam turbine generators:** ~25% of TDPS revenue; market growing 10-12% (captive power, biomass, waste-heat); machine sizes shifting from 30MW to 60MW range.
- **Gas turbine & gas engine generators:** "massive growth continues without pause"; large-volume orders; notable delivery into SpaceX projects; current volume orders are sub-50MW. Strong forecast through FY28.
- **Hydro:** one of TDPS's highest hydro years ahead; active in refurbishment in India and abroad; high-value wins expected this/next quarter.
- **Motors:** deprioritized in FY26 in favour of high-volume export generators; separating manufacturing lines for focus; expects stabilization and improving traction. Includes NPCIL induction-motor order (nuclear, slow/choppy ordering).
- **Railway:** orders across US, Europe, Russia + India (4 markets next year); "nothing new to report."
- **Subsidiaries:** DFPS fully written down; UK R&D sub (100%) drives large-generator technology (no royalty, captive); Turkey plant for small Turkish-market machines + EU service backup.

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Built on acquired and licensed technology: "Acquires Technology from Toyo Denki Japan" (1999-2001), vertical hydro generators developed "with VOITH, Germany", a long-term supply agreement with INNIO for gas engine generators, and a "License Agreement with Siemens to produce 2 pole Generators up to 250MVA" (2012).
- "Becomes the market leader in India" (2002-09); a 2021 milestone notes "Revival in the Domestic market with increased Brand Recognition Globally".
- Installed base as on 30.06.2026 of "8375 Units (Including Made in Turkey Generators)" across "Countries 113", with "New country added is Bahamas"; the MD's bio cites product reach "to over 98 countries".
- The gas-turbine segment commentary states the wins are "Positions TDPS as a strategic global manufacturing partner in high-volume, export-driven programs."
- Achieved "Highest Revenue & PAT For the third consecutive year" (2026 milestone), following "Highest Revenue & PAT since inception" in 2024.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Guidance] "The outlook for FY 27 and FY 28 is strong, the company has upgraded its FY 27 guidance to Rs 2,600 crores."
- [Order book] Order Book on 30th June 2026 of Rs 22,073 Million; the deck also states "The current rate of order inflow has exceeded Rs. 700 crores per quarter and this puts pressure squarely on execution and the company is well positioned to deliver close to the inflow rate."
- [Export skew] "93% of order inflow in Q1 FY'27 is from Exports" — Rs 6,836 Mn v/s Rs 2,573 Mn.
- [Segment wins] Hydro: "Secured the segment's largest order from a Domestic Hydro OEM for 4 x 16 MW vertical hydro generators for a major hydropower project in Africa." Steam: multiple Captive Power Plant orders from a major turbine OEM "including a 60 MW, 2-pole range generator, among the largest in the segment". Gas engine: a domestic OEM order for a "~6 MW machine for India's largest LNG terminal".
- [Pipeline] Gas turbine volume orders secured from a major global OEM in the "14-18 MW range, multi-project", with a "Strong expected large-order pipeline from a second major global OEM across the 12-19 MW ratings for US programs"; further high-volume genset programs indicated for CY-2027 plus an expected competitor-replacement order for an African mining customer.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body:
- Gross contribution historically 33-34%; Q4 ~3% below due to Turkey LD; reverting to ~34%.
- RM basket: copper, forgings, electrical steel, mild steel, insulating materials (copper share not disclosed).
- Copper "drastic" (~$14,000); hedges running out → new customer prices kicking in unevenly. Protected via RM hedges + price-variation clauses.
- FX: high export exposure gives rupee-devaluation tailwind that offsets dollar/euro RM imports → broadly currency-neutral / margin-neutral.
- Sudden 10-15% commodity spikes can't be fully passed through immediately (customers won't reprice in a week); manageable for next 2-3 quarters; risk if commodities jump another 20-30%.
- Employee costs largely stable QoQ; "largely employed everyone we want" — no major additions ahead.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

latest_quarter.body:
- **FY27 guidance raised** to INR2,400 cr+ with explicit upside bias; FY28 framed at ~INR32 bn (capacity-bound).
- **New large-generator capex program announced** (up to 200MW) — fresh strategic signal; detailed numbers promised in 2-3 months; ramp FY29.
- **First-ever CEO hire** (Deepak, ex-L&T Mitsubishi / GE) — governance/professionalization milestone.
- **Turkey LD one-off** dented Q4 consol gross margin ~3% (vs 33-34% norm) — non-recurring.
- **DFPS subsidiary** investment fully written down (final INR30 mn provided).
- **Order inflow inflected sharply:** Q4 +61%, FY26 +51%; pending generator+motor order +66% YoY.
- **SpaceX** newly named as a delivery destination.
- **Copper inflation** newly flagged as the key margin watch-item as hedges roll off.
latest_quarter.title: QoQ change log

outlook.body:
- **FY27 revenue:** revised up to INR2,400 cr+ (24 bn+), with "extremely high probability" of a further upward revision to match Q4 inflow run-rate.
- **FY28:** capacity to address INR32 bn; mgmt expects ~INR32-33 bn on a conservative basis ("retained earnings all going into working capital").
- **Order book growth:** no formal FY28 inflow guidance, but conservatively +20-25% next year over this year.
- **Margins FY27:** in line with FY26, slightly better excluding the Turkey one-off; gross contribution to revert to ~34% historical average.
- **Q1 FY27:** progress so far suggests it will beat Q4 of last FY.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body:
- Mfg order book INR19.73 bn: Generators 16.77 bn · Railway 2.47 bn · Spares/aftermarket 0.2 bn · Turkey 0.29 bn.
- Export + deemed-export share of book ~76% (ex-railway).
- Q4 export inflow 80% of total (INR5.28 bn). FY26 export+deemed inflow 17.33 bn (+76% YoY); 79% of full-year inflow is exports, 21% domestic.
- Pending generator+motor order grew 66% FY26 vs FY25.
- ~INR2,000 cr of pending order to be executed this year (FY27).
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body:
- **Large generators (up to 200MW):** the headline optionality. Existing stator line was built in 2012-13; rotor side under-invested 15 yrs ago — now investing heavily in rotor manufacturing + large machining centers. Targets export (power gen, large AI data centers, combined-cycle, potentially SMR/nuclear in ~200MW range). Detailed business plan/numbers in ~2-3 months.
- **AI data center power:** US alone ~100 GW over 5-7 yrs; could ~double globally — long cycle.
- **SMR / nuclear:** TDPS caps at ~200MW; if SMRs land in that range, addressable.
- **Aeroderivative engine generator prototype:** in progress with a customer (no specifics disclosed).
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: A pure-play generator-maker plugged deep into the global gas-turbine/engine OEM supply chain (INNIO, Baker Hughes, SpaceX projects), riding a multi-year AI-data-center + power-gen capex super-cycle with 76-79% export mix, now committing to a large-generator (up to 200MW) capacity build that opens a much bigger TAM from FY29.

drhp.business: TD Power Systems Limited designs and manufactures AC generators for steam, gas, hydro, and diesel power plants, alongside synchronous, induction, and traction motors for industrial and mobility applications. The company supplies to leading global OEMs, utilities, and EPC contractors, with products installed in over 113 countries. It operates manufacturing facilities in Bengaluru, India, and an international presence in Turkey.

The only investment-related note is a provision for diminution in the value of investment in its subsidiary D F Power Systems Private Limited.
